8.1 IN GENERAL THE MINIMUM PERIOD BEFORE STRIKING FORM WORK SHALL BE AS PER CL. 11.3 OF IS 456. THE PERIOD MAY BE VARIED AFTER PROPER EVALUATION OF THE CONCRETE TEST RESULTS AND IN SUCH CASES THE RESULTS SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO THE CONSULTANT FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. 8.2 STRIPPING & CYCLE TIME FOR PT SLABS / FLAT SLABS, IF ANY, SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO THE CONSULTANT FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. 8.3 ALL FORM WORK AND PROPS UNDER SUSPENDED CONCRETE WORKS SHALL BE REMOVED BEFORE COMMENCEMENT OF MASONRY WORK. 8.4 SIMPLY SUPPORTED AND CONTINUOUS SPANS SHALL BE STRIPPED FROM MID SPAN TOWARDS SUPPORTS. 8.5 CANTILEVER SPANS SHALL BE STRIPPED FROM THE FREE END PROCEEDING GRADUALLY TOWARDS THE SUPPORT. 8.6 WATER TANK BASE SLAB FORM WORK SHALL BE REMOVED ONLY AFTER REMOVAL OF TANK COVER SLAB FORMWORK.

7.1 ALL LAPS FOR STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS SHALL BE AS PER DESIGN DRAWINGS ONLY AND MAXIMUM LENGTH OF BARS AVAILABLE IN THE MARKET SHALL BE USED TO REDUCE ADDITIONAL LAPS APART FROM DESIGN LAPS. THE FOLLOWING GUIDELINES SHALL BE REFERRED ONLY FOR PLANNING THE ADDITIONAL LAPS, IF ANY REQUIRED AS PER SITE CONDITION AT THE DISCRETION OF THE SITE ENGINEER.. 7.1.a LAPS SHALL BE STAGGERED SUCH THAT NOT MORE THAN 50%OF REINFORCEMENT IS LAPPED AT ANY LOCATION AND THE CENTRE TO CENTRE DISTANCE BETWEEN SUCH LAPS SHALL BE ATLEAST 1.30 TIMES THE LAP LENGTH OR AS INDICATED IN DRAWING. 7.1.b TOP BARS IN BEAMS & SLABS SHALL BE LAPPED AT MIDDLE ONE -THIRD OF SPAN AND NOT AT SUPPORT ZONE. 7.1.c BOTTOM BARS IN BEAMS & SLABS SHALL BE LAPPED NEAR END ONE -THIRD SPAN. 7.2 HOOKS OR BENDS SHALL BE PROVIDED AS PER STANDARD DETAILS WHEREVER NECESSARY FOR REINFORCEMENTS IN BEAMS, COLUMNS, SLABS, ETC. 7.3 THE FOLLOWING MINIMUM LAP LENGTHS, IN MM, SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR REINFORCEMENT IN FLEXURAL TENSION.

9.1 CONSTRUCTION JOINT LOCATIONS SHALL BE PLANNED, DETAILED ALONG WITH SUITABLE BONDING AGENTS AND SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO THE CONSULTANT FOR APPROVAL. HOWEVER, THE FOLLOWING PARAMETERS MAY BE FOLLOWED AS A GENERAL GUIDELINE DURING THE PLANNING STAGE. 9.2 SLABS : AT SPAN/3 FROM SUPPORT. 9.3 BEAMS : AT SPAN/3 FROM SUPPORT. IF ANY CROSS BEAMS ARE LOCATED IN THIS REGION THE JOINT SHALL BE LOCATED TWO TIMES THE WIDTH OF THE CROSS BEAM AWAY FROM THE SUPPORT. 9.4 RETAINING WALL : NEAR THE JUNCTION OF THE WALL AND FOOTING WITH A KEY JOINT. 9.5 RAFT SLAB : AT SPAN/3 FROM SUPPORT. 9.6 CANTILEVERS : CONSTRUCTION JOINTS NOT ALLOWED UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED BY THE CONSULTANT

1.1 ALL DIMENSIONS NOTED IN THE DRAWINGS ARE IN MILLIMETRES & LEVELS ARE IN METRES UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. 1.2 ALL DIMENSIONS AND LEVELS OF PERMANENT & TEMPORARY WORKS (TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION SITE SET BACKS, REFERENCE BENCH MARKS ETC., ) SHALL BE VERIFIED AT SITE PRIOR TO START OF WORK. 1.3 ANY DISCREPANCY IN DRAWINGS SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT / EDRC BEFORE COMMENCING WORK. 1.4 ALL STRUCTURAL DRAWINGS SHALL BE READ IN CONJUNCTION WITH RELEVANT AND LATEST ARCHITECTURAL AND MEP SERVICE DRAWINGS. 1.5 DIMENSIONS MENTIONED IN THE DRAWINGS SHALL ONLY BE USED. DO NOT SCALE DRAWINGS.

2.1 EXCAVATION IN VARIOUS TYPES OF SOIL PROFILE SHALL BE EXECUTED AS PER PROPERLY ENGINEERED SCHEMES DULY APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT. SCHEME SHALL INCLUDE TEMPORARY RETAINING MEASURES COMPRISING SHORING, STRUTTING, BRACING, ETC. ALONG WITH DEWATERING AND BACKFILLING SEQUENCE. 2.2 EXCAVATION USING MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT SHALL BE STOPPED 150mm ABOVE FOUNDATION LEVEL AND THE REMAINING PORTION SHALL BE MANUALLY DRESSED TO AVOID DISTURBANCE OF FOUNDATION STRATA. 2.3 EXCAVATION FOR FOUNDATIONS SHALL BE DONE UPTO THE LEVEL SHOWN IN THE DRAWING AND THE SOIL PROFILE BE REVIEWED BY FIELD EXPERT TO CONFIRM THAT THE SOIL PROFILE HAS THE MENTIONED SBC. IF THE RECOMMENDED SBC IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THE MENTIONED LEVEL, SAME SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF CONSULTANT AND UPON INSTRUCTIONS, EXCAVATION SHALL PROCEED UPTO THE REQUIRED DEPTH TO ACHIEVE THE RECOMMENDED SBC AND THE DIFFERENCE IN LEVEL SHALL BE BACK FILLED AS PER RECOMMENDATION. 2.4 IF GOOD STRATA IS MET AT A DEPTH EARLIER THAN SPECIFIED IN THE DRAWING, SAME SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT FOR NECESSARY REVIEW. 2.5 EXCESS EXCAVATION / UNDULATION BELOW FOUNDATION SHALL BE BACK FILLED AS PER SPECIFICATIONS . 2.6 ORGANIC MATTER LIKE ROOTS , VEGETATIONS, ETC IF FOUND BELOW FOUNDATION LEVEL SHALL BE COMPLETELY REMOVED AND BACK FILLED AS PER SPECIFICATIONS. 2.7 EXISTING WELL, SUMP, SEPTIC TANK, IF ANY, AT SITE SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT AND FOUNDATIONS, IF ANY, PLANNED ABOVE / NEAR THE SAME SHALL BE CAST AS INSTRUCTED BY THE CONSULTANT. 2.8 BACK FILLING OF SOIL ADJACENT TO RETAINING WALL SHALL BE DONE STRICTLY AS MENTIONED IN RETAINING WALL NUMERATION DRAWINGS (TO ENSURE PROP ACTION IF REQUIRED) AND VEHICLE MOVEMENT ADJACENT TO THE RETAINING WALL SHALL BE PERMITTED AFTER THE STRUCTURE HAS ATTAINED ITS DESIGN STRENGTH. 2.9 FILLING IN BETWEEN FOUNDATIONS SHALL BE WITH SELECTED EARTH AND AS PER SPECIFICATIONS APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT. 2.10 FILLING UPTO PLINTH LEVEL SHALL BE WITH SELECTED EARTH AND AS PER SPECIFICATIONS APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT

11.1 STACKING OF CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL AND VEHICULAR MOVEMENT ON FLOOR SLAB,SHALL BE AVOIDED IF ANY, SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT. 11.2 CORE CUT & WALL CHASING IN RC WALL, IF ANY, SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT BEFORE CARRYING OUT THE WORK AT SITE.

6.1 TEST RESULTS FOR REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE OBTAINED FROM REPUTED TESTING LABORATORIES (PREFERABLY ACCREDITED BY NABL - NATIONAL ACCREDITATION BOARD OF LABORATORIES)\~ AND APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT OR QA /QC TEAM BEFORE USING THE REINFORCEMENT AT SITE. 6.2 THE GRADE OF REINFORCEMENT OF INDIVIDUAL ELEMENTS SHALL BE REFERRED FROM RESPECTIVE STRUCTURAL GOOD FOR CONSTRUCTION (GFC) / ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION (IFC) DRAWINGS AND SHALL CONFORM TO IS : 1786. 6.3 REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE BENT AND FIXED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROCEDURE AS SPECIFIED IN IS: 2502. 6.4 ALL THE REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE PLACED AND MAINTAINED IN POSITION AS SHOWN IN THE DRAWINGS. 6.5 BARS SHALL BE HELD & TIED IN POSITION BY USING BINDING WIRES NOT GREATER THAN 18 GAUGE ANNEALED ONLY AND NO WELDING IS PERMITTED FOR BARS UPTO 32 DIA. INCASE OF BARS GREATER THAN 32 DIA WELDING SCHEMES AS APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT SHALL BE ADOPTED. 6.6 ALL BAR SPACINGS ARE MARKED TO THE CENTER LINES OF THE BARS UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. 6.7 GENERALLY THE REINFORCEMENT BARS OF DIAMETER AS SPECIFIED IN THE DRAWINGS SHALL ONLY BE USED. IN EXCEPTIONAL CASES OF NON-AVAILABILTY OF PARTICULAR DIAMETER, SAME SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE CONSULTANT AND UPON APPROVAL, BARS OF OTHER DIAMETER MAY BE USED. 6.8 HEATING OF THE REINFORCEMENT BARS ARE NOT PERMITTED FOR BENDING. 6.9 SUPPORTS FOR FORM WORK SHALL NOT BE TAKEN FROM THE REINFORCEMENT BARS.

3.1 PROPERLY ENGINEERED FORM WORK SCHEMES SHALL BE ADOPTED FOR ALL STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS. INCASE OF FLAT SLABS, POST TENSIONED SLABS / BEAMS, LARGE SPAN STRUCTURES, CANTILEVERS, DOUBLE HEIGHT FLOORS AND OTHER SPECIAL STRUCTURES, THE SCHEMES SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO THE CONSULTANT FOR REVIEW. 3.2 THE FORM WORK SHALL BE DESIGNED AND CONSTRUCTED SO AS TO REMAIN SUFFICIENTLY RIGID DURING PLACING AND COMPACTION OF CONCRETE AND SHALL BE SUCH AS TO PREVENT LOSS OF SLURRY FROM THE CONCRETE. 3.3 THE TYPE OF FORM WORK SHALL BE CHOSEN BASED ON THE FINAL FINISH (FORM FINISH / PLASTER FINISH) OF THE ELEMENT AS PER ARCHITECTURAL INTENT. 3.4 PRE-CAMBER, IF ANY, SHALL BE PROVIDED TO THE FLOOR SLABS / BEAMS AS SPECIFIED IN THE RELEVANT DRAWINGS .

4.1 MATERIAL : 4.1.a CEMENT USED FOR ALL CONCRETE WORKS SHALL BE ORDINARY PORTLAND CEMENT (43 GRADE OR 53 GRADE) OR PORTLAND POZZOLONA CEMENT OR PORTLAND SLAG CEMENT UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. 4.1.b FLYASH / GROUND GRANULATED BLAST FURNACE SLAG USED, IF ANY, AS\~ PART REPLACEMENT TO CEMENT SHALL CONFORM TO IS 3812 (PART 1) AND THE PERCENTAGE ADDITION SHALL BE AS PER PROVISIONS OF IS 456. 4.1.c TWO DIFFERENT CEMENT BRANDS SHALL NOT BE USED IN THE SAME POUR OR WITH IN SAME STRUCTURAL ELEMENT. 4.1.d COARSE AND FINE AGGREGATE USED SHALL CONFORM TO IS 383. THE MAXIMUM SIZE OF AGGREGATE SHALL PREFERABLY BE 20, 25 & 80/40 DOWNGRADED FOR RCC, PCC\~ AND\~ PLUM\~CONCRETE RESPECTIVELY, UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. 4.1.e ADMIXTURES USED, IF ANY, SHALL CONFORM TO IS 9103. HOWEVER\~ ACCELERATORS SHALL NOT BE USED IN STRUCTURAL CONCRETE WITHOUT PRIOR APPROVAL FROM THE CONSULTANT. 4.2 MIX : 4.2.a THE GRADE OF CONCRETE OF INDIVIDUAL ELEMENTS SHALL BE REFERRED FROM RESPECTIVE STRUCTURAL GOOD FOR CONSTRUCTION (GFC) / ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION (IFC) DRAWINGS. 4.2.b ALL CONCRETE SHALL BE OF DESIGN MIX CONFORMING TO THE PROVISIONS OF TABLE 5 OF IS 456 AND TEST RESULTS BE OBTAINED FROM REPUTED\~ TESTING LABORATORIES\~(PREFERABLY ACCREDITED BY NABL - NATIONAL ACCREDITATION BOARD OF LABORATORIES)\~ AND APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT OR QA/QC TEAM AT SITE. 4.2.c SULPHATE RESISTING CEMENT CONCRETE , IF USED, SHALL CONFORM TO PROVISIONS OF TABLE 4 OF IS 456. 4.2.d THE JUNCTION OF TWO ELEMENTS HAVING DIFFERENT GRADES OF CONCRETE MIX SHALL HAVE HIGHER GRADE OF CONCRETE MIX UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. 4.2.e SLUMP OF CONCRETE SHALL BE AS FOLLOWS UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. I. FOUNDATIONS : 100 ± 25 II. PILE FOUNDATIONS : 150 TO 180 III. PUMPING CONCRETE (FOR ALL STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS EXCEPT PILES AND FOUNDATIONS) : 125 ± 25 4.2.f SELF COMPACTING CONCRETE, IF USED IN THE PROJECT, SHALL CONFORM TO PROVISIONS OF EUROPEAN FEDERATION OF NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS REPRESENTING FOR CONCRETE (EFNARC) SPECIFICATION-2005. 4.2.g ALL CONCRETE MIX INGREDIENTS SHALL BE WEIGH BATCHED AND MIXED IN FULLY AUTOMATED BATCHING PLANT. USE OF VOLUMETRIC BATCHING IS NOT PERMITTED UNLESS APPROVED BY THE CONSULTANT OR THE QA/QC TEAM AT SITE.

MASS CONCRETING SHALL BE DONE FOR LINAC TO PREVENT RADIATION. WHEN LARGE VOLUME OF CONCRETE IS PLACED, THERE IS A DANGER OF THERMAL CRACKING BECAUSE OF RESTRAINT TO CONTRACTION ON COOLING FROM PEAK TEMPERATURE CAUSED BY THE HEAT OF HYDRATION OF CEMENT. WHEN CONCRETE MASS IS NOT INSULATED FROM THE ATMOSPHERE, TEMPERATURE GRADIENT EXISTS WITHIN THE CONCRETE BECAUSE ITS INTERIOR BECOMES HOT, WHILE THE SURFACE LOSES HEAT TO THE ATMOSPHERE WHICH CREATES TENSILE STRESS AT THE SURFACE AND CAUSES THERMAL CRACKING. TO PREVENT THERMAL CRACKING IN MASS CONCRETING, THE FOLLOWING PROCESS SHALL BE ADOPTED.

1.1 REDUCE THE HEAT OF HYDRATION BY OPTIMIZING THE CEMENTITIOUS MATERIAL COMPOSITION USING SUPPLEMENTRY CEMENTITIOUS MATERIAL SUCH AS FLY ASH OR SLAG OR LOW HEAT CEMENT OR BLENDED HYDRAULIC CEMENT OR GROUND GRANULATED BLAST FURNACE SLAG IN THE MIX DESIGN. 1.2 SPRINKLING OF WATER OVER THE AGGREGATES, CRUSHED ICE CUBES OR CHILLED WATER IN CONCRETE CAN BE USED AS PER MIX DESIGNER'S RECOMMENDATIONS. 1.3 THE LOWEST PRACTICAL CEMENT CONTENT PERMITTED BY STRENGTH AND DURABILITY REQUIREMENTS GIVEN IN IS CODE SHOULD BE USED TO REDUCE THE HEAT OF HYDRATION. 1.4 MINOR HAIR LINE CRACKS LESS THAN 0.2MM DUE TO RESTRAINTS CONSIDERED.

2.1 INSULATE THE CONCRETE SURFACE FROM ATMOSPHERIC TEMPERATURE i.e.., BY KEEPING THERMOCOL FIXED AS INSULATION PANEL AT THE SIDES ALONG WITH FORMWORK AND TOP SURFACE OF CONCRETE IS COVERED WITH POLYSTYRENE SHEET WITH A LAYER OF SAND, SO THAT THE TEMPERATURE VARIATION BETWEEN CONCRETE INNER CORE AND SURFACE CAN BE REDUCED. 2.2 VERTICAL WALL SHOULD BE TAKEN IN EITHER ONE OR TWO LIFTS (WALL HEIGHT/2 FOR EACH LIFT) AS PER APPROVED METHOD OF STATEMENT. 2.3 IN CASE OF SUDDEN RAIN, PLASTIC SHEETING SHALL BE USED TO COVER THE CONCRETING AREA. 2.4 DESHUTTERING OF WALL SHALL BE DONE WHEN THE DIFFERENTIAL TEMPERATURE BETWEEN CONCRETE INNER CORE AND SURFACE IS LESS THAN APPROXIMATELY AND WHEN THE AMBIENT TEMPERATURE IS AT ITS PEAK.

3.1 CONCRETE TEMPERATURE SHALL BE CHECKED AT THE TIME OF PLACING. CONCRETING CAN BE DONE PREFERABLY IN THE EVENING AND NIGHT (NOT DURING HOT SUNNY WEATHER) TO REDUCE CONCRETE POUR TEMPERATURE (CONCRETE PLACING TEMPERATURE SHALL BE LESS THEN MAXIMUM) 3.2 THE TEMPERATURE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN INNER CORE TEMPERATURE AND SURFACE TEMPERATURE SHALL BE LESS THAN AND IT IS TO BE MEASURED BY EITHER THERMOCOUPLES OR ELECTRONIC SENSORS EMBEDDED IN THE INTERIOR AND SURFACE OF CONCRETE. THE FORMWORK INSULATION THICKNESS SHALL BE DESIGNED ACCORDINGLY. 3.3 THERMOCOUPLE NEED TO BE INSTALLED IN PREDEFINED LOCATION BEFORE CONCRETING AND TEMPERATURE MONITERING SHALL BE DONE AT FREQUENT INTERVALS. 3.4 CONSTRUCTION JOINT: IT HAS TO BE PROPERLY TREATED WITH SBR LATEX (1:1:3 = SBR:WATER:CEMENT) AND SHEAR KEYS FOR ENSURING PROPER BOND. 3.5 CONCRETING SHALL BE CARRIED OUT IN FREQUENT LAYERS NOT MORE THAN 450MM THICK TO AVOID THE COLD JOINT. (REFER FIGURE-1) 3.6 FREE HEIGHT OF FALL OF CONCRETE SHALL BE RESTRICTED TO 3.0M 3.7 GOOD COMPACTION OF CONCRETE AS PER IS CODAL PROVISIONS SHALL BE ASSURED BY APPROPRIATE QA/QC METHODS. 3.8 CONCRETE PLACEMENT AND COMPACTION SHALL BE ENSURED TO AVOID SEGREGATION AND HONEY COMBING.
